en: On the first day of the Ten Uposatha Days of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva,
the Youth descends; by reciting the name of Dīpaṃkara Tathāgata and observing the fast, one shall be spared from the Hell of Unanointed Swords and Spears and have the sins of forty kalpas eliminated.

On the eighth day, when the Prince descended to contemplate the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light Buddha, those in the Hell of Excrement and Filth who maintained the fast were cleared of their offenses for thirty kalpas.

On the fourteenth day, when he surveyed the Lord of Life and descended to contemplate the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, those in the Hell of Boiling Cauldrons who maintained the fast were cleared of their offenses for one thousand kalpas.

On the fifteenth day, the Great General of the Five Paths descends; by reciting the name of Amitābha Buddha and observing the fast, one will not fall into the Cold Ice Hell and shall have the sins of two hundred kalpas eliminated.

On the eighteenth day, King Yama descends; by reciting the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and observing the fast, one will not fall into the Sword-Tree Hell and shall have the sins of ninety kalpas eliminated.

On the twenty-third day, the Great General descends; by reciting the name of Vairocana Buddha, one shall not fall into the realm of hungry ghosts or the hells, and by observing the fast, one's sins for a thousand kalpas shall be eliminated.

On the twenty-fourth day, the Lord of Mount Tai descends; by reciting the name of the Bodhisattva of the Hells, one shall not fall into the Hell of Chopping and Slicing, and by observing the fast, one's sins for a thousand kalpas shall be eliminated.
On the twenty-eighth day, Śakra descended; by recollecting Amitābha Buddha and observing the fast, one avoids falling into the Iron Saw Hell and eliminates the sins of ninety kalpas.

On the twenty-ninth day, the Four Heavenly Kings descend; by recollecting Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva and observing the fast, one avoids falling into the Grinding Stone Hell and eliminates the sins of seven thousand kalpas.

On the thirtieth day, Brahmādeva descended and thought of Śākyamuni Buddha; by observing the fast, he was spared from falling into the Ashes Hell and had his offenses removed for eight thousand kalpas.
